claim: Even in Ebola infections, 40% of infected people survive.
source: even in Ebola infections, 40% of infected people survive, Shultz et al., 2016
evidence: Supported by citation to Shultz et al., 2016

claim: Hosts can survive an infection by strategies which combine resisting to pathogens by producing immune defense and tolerating the consequences of infection.
source: Overall, the hosts can, therefore, survive an infection by strategies which combine resisting to pathogens by producing immune defense and tolerating the consequences of infection (in animals Ayres and Schneider, 2008; Råberg et al., 2007; Read et al., 2008, but also in plants Kover and Schaal, 2002).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to empirical work in animals and plants

claim: Immune defense is a double-edged sword which can save the host's life but sometimes cause pathologies and reduce lifespan.
source: For example, immune defense is a double-edged sword which can save the host's life but sometimes cause pathologies and reduce lifespan (Critchlow et al., 2023; Lin et al., 2018; Petkau et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Invertebrates share with mammals a large part of the mechanisms underlying their innate immune system, as shown in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Second, they share with mammals a large part of the mechanisms underlying their innate immune system, as shown in Drosophila melanogaster (Buchon et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Buchon et al., 2014

claim: The model predicts that infections can stabilize at a Set-Point Pathogen Load (SPPL) when chronic.
source: When chronic, infections stabilize at a Set-Point Pathogen Load (SPPL).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model presented in the manuscript

claim: The SPPL can be transient, being then a predictor of life span which depends on initial condition (e.g. inoculum).
source: Our model predicts that this situation can be transient, the SPPL being then a predictor of life span which depends on initial condition (e.g. inoculum).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model

claim: When stable, the SPPL is diagnostic of non-lethal chronic infections.
source: When stable, the SPPL is rather diagnostic of non-lethal chronic infections.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model

claim: In lethal infections, hosts die at a Pathogen Load Upon Death (PLUD) which is almost independent from the initial conditions.
source: In lethal infections, hosts die at a Pathogen Load Upon Death (PLUD) which is almost independent from the initial conditions.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model

claim: The PLUD can be used in conjunction with mortality measurement to distinguish the effect of disease tolerance from that of resistance.
source: we demonstrate that it can be used in conjunction with mortality measurement to distinguish the effect of disease tolerance from that of resistance.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model analysis

claim: Hosts that were wounded had a higher PLUD.
source: We found that, as predicted by the model, hosts that were wounded or deficient of key antimicrobial peptides had a higher PLUD
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Hosts deficient of key antimicrobial peptides had a higher PLUD.
source: We found that, as predicted by the model, hosts that were wounded or deficient of key antimicrobial peptides had a higher PLUD
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Catalase mutant hosts, likely to have a default in disease tolerance, had a lower PLUD.
source: while Catalase mutant hosts, likely to have a default in disease tolerance, had a lower PLUD.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript

claim: Bistability in WHD models can be created by non-linear functional responses for both pathogen dynamics and host defense regulation.
source: Mayer et al., 1995 demonstrated that in such models non-linear functional responses for both pathogen dynamics and host defense regulation could yield bifurcations between chronic infections with high and low equilibrium pathogen load.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mayer et al., 1995

claim: The model can reproduce infections which range from chronic to acute and from benign to lethal.
source: We found that only models with complex, non-linear regulations of immunity can satisfactorily reproduce infections which range from chronic to acute and from benign to lethal.
evidence: This is a finding from the model analysis

claim: The model adequately predicts both the existence and the properties of the SPPL if defense production is assumed to decrease with accumulating damage.
source: We further demonstrated that the model adequately predicts both the existence and the properties of the SPPL if defense production is assumed to decrease with accumulating damage.
evidence: This is a finding from the model analysis

claim: The SPPL can be transient and predict the host's lifespan.
source: We show that the SPPL can then be transient and does, as documented in HIV infections, predict the host's lifespan.
evidence: This is a model prediction supported by comparison to HIV infection data

claim: The PLUD is virtually independent of inoculum size.
source: Our model also predicts that the host dies at a PLUD which is virtually independent of inoculum size (as observed by Duneau et al., 2017a)
evidence: This is a model prediction that matches empirical observations

claim: The PLUD should reflect the genetic characteristics of interacting pathogens and hosts.
source: and should therefore reflect the genetic characteristics of interacting pathogens and hosts.
evidence: This is an inference from the model's prediction about PLUD independence from initial conditions

claim: Empirical evidence of bistability indicates that the infection lowers the immune defense either directly or indirectly through resource diversion or damage accumulation.
source: We, therefore, propose that empirical evidence of bistability, such as in Figure 1, indicate that the infection lowers the immune defense either directly, as in Ellner et al., 2021, or indirectly, through resource diversion, as in van Leeuwen et al., 2019, or damage accumulation, as in our model.
evidence: This is an inference from the model combined with citations to other theoretical work

claim: The SPPL depends on initial inoculum when Drosophila are infected by pathogenic bacteria.
source: These results are in line with empirical results, as the SPPL depends on initial inoculum when Drosophila are infected by pathogenic bacteria (Chambers et al., 2019; Duneau et al., 2017a; Acuña Hidalgo et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citations to empirical studies

claim: The SPPL does not depend on initial inoculum when Drosophila are infected by non-pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli.
source: but not when infected by non-pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli (Ramirez-Corona et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to empirical study

claim: Testing the link between the SPPL and the initial dose is a way to experimentally demonstrate that the control over infection is transient.
source: We, therefore, propose that testing the link between the SPPL and the initial dose is a way to experimentally demonstrate that the control over infection is transient.
evidence: This is a proposed experimental method based on model predictions

claim: The PLUD increases when resistance is diminished.
source: Another particularity of the PLUD, is that it increases when resistance is diminished (red curves in Figure 5C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by model simulations shown in Figure 5C

claim: The PLUD decreases when tolerance is lowered.
source: but decreases when tolerance is lowered (blue curves in Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by model simulations shown in Figure 5C

claim: Variations in parameters which have a direct impact on the dynamics of damage produce a negative correlation between PLUD and HR.
source: As a result, variations in parameters which have a direct impact on the dynamics of damage produce a negative correlation between PLUD and HR.
evidence: This is an inference from the elasticity analysis of the model

claim: Variations in parameters that control the defense result in a positive correlation between the PLUD and HR.
source: Variations in parameters that control the defense, therefore, result in a positive correlation between the PLUD and HR.
evidence: This is an inference from the elasticity analysis of the model

claim: Faster death would indicate lower tolerance when associated with lower PLUD.
source: In summary, Figure 6 indicates that faster death (i.e. increased HR) would indicate lower tolerance when associated with lower PLUD
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis shown in Figure 6

claim: Faster death would suggest lower resistance in case of higher PLUD.
source: when it would rather suggest lower resistance in case of higher PLUD.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis shown in Figure 6

claim: The wound significantly reduced survival in Drosophila melanogaster infected with Providencia rettgeri.
source: We found that indeed, the wound significantly reduced survival (Cox proportional hazard model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 1397.44, degrees of freedom (df) = 1, p - value < 2.2e-16).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: Wounded hosts die at a PLUD significantly higher than non-wounded hosts.
source: We found in both analyses that wounded hosts die at a PLUD significantly higher than non-wounded (linear mixed model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 11.29, df = 1, p - value = 0.008 with outliers removed; X2 = 11.04, df = 1, p - value = 0.0009 with outliers retained)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: The wound increases both hazard ratio and PLUD.
source: Overall the wound does increase both hazard ratio and PLUD, as our model predicts.
evidence: Supported by experimental data that confirms model predictions

claim: Inflicting damage to D. melanogaster hinders the production of defense, and thus indirectly reduces resistance.
source: This result can be taken as an evidence that inflicting damage to D. melanogaster hinders the production of defense, and thus indirectly reduces resistance.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental results

claim: The PLUD exhibited an increase when the Imd pathway was suppressed.
source: We observed that the PLUD exhibited an increase when the Imd pathway was suppressed (Kruskal-Wallis: X2 = 7.87, df = 1, p-value = 0.005)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: The PLUD exhibited an increase when melanization was inhibited.
source: or when melanization was inhibited (Kruskal-Wallis: X2 = 15.56, df = 1, p-value = 7.9e-5).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: There was no significant change in PLUD when the Toll pathway was suppressed.
source: However, there was no significant change in PLUD when the Toll pathway was suppressed (Kruskal-Wallis: X2 = 0.03, df = 1, p-value = 0.86).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data

claim: Lines A, B, and AB have higher death rates when infected by P. rettgeri compared to line BomΔ55C.
source: We found that, compared to line BomΔ55C, lines A, B, and AB have higher death rates when infected by P. rettgeri (Figure 8A; Cox proportional hazard model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 138.12, df = 3, p-value = 9.6e-30)
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 8A

claim: Lines A, B, and AB have higher PLUD compared to line BomΔ55C.
source: and higher PLUD (Figure 8B; linear mixed model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 17.01, df = 3 , p-value = 0.0007).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 8B

claim: Deleting Diptericin A makes the mutant more susceptible to P. rettgeri infection than Drs mutant.
source: (D) demonstrates that deleting Diptericin A is sufficient to make the mutant more susceptible to the infection than Drs mutant.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D

claim: Deleting Diptericin A increases the PLUD.
source: (E and F) demonstrate that this increase in susceptibility goes together with an increase in PLUD.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E and F

claim: Silencing Diptericin A accelerates death.
source: Silencing Diptericin A accelerates death (G)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8G

claim: Silencing Diptericin A significantly increases the PLUD.
source: and significantly increases the PLUD (H-I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8H-I

claim: A reduction in resistance caused by a lack of effectors provokes an increase in both HR and PLUD.
source: Overall, based on previous results and on those three different approaches, we concluded that a reduction in resistance caused by a lack of effectors provokes an increase in both HR and PLUD.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental approaches

claim: The increase in PLUD is remarkably constant throughout experiments (approx. +0.2) even though the HR varies from approx. +0.3 to +1.5.
source: Finally, it should be noticed that, as our model predicts, the increase in PLUD is remarkably constant throughout experiments (approx. +0.2 in Figure 8C, F and I) even though the HR varies from approx. +0.3 to +1.5.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 8

claim: Catalase is among several enzymes involved in scavenging oxygen free radicals and protecting cells.
source: Catalase is among several enzymes involved in scavenging oxygen free radicals and protecting those cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Catalase function

claim: The activity of Catalases into reducing reactive oxygen species has been shown in Drosophila infections.
source: The activity of Catalases into reducing reactive oxygen species has been shown in Drosophila infections (Ha et al., 2005)
evidence: Supported by citation to Ha et al., 2005

claim: Silencing Catalase increases flies susceptibility to systemic bacterial infection.
source: We found that silencing Catalase ubiquitously with Actin-Gal4 driving an RNAi does increase flies susceptibility to systemic bacterial infection when comparing to a match genetic background as control (i.e. attP2 control line, the advised RNAi control for the attP2 genetic background of the TRiP genetic RNAi panel, see Figure 9A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A

claim: Silencing Catalase decreases the PLUD.
source: We further observed that silencing Catalase does decrease the PLUD (see Figure 9B; linear mixed model with random experimental blocks and a correction for heteroscedasticity: X2 = 23.33, df = 1, p-value = 1.37e-6).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 9B

claim: Catalase is part of the arsenal that enable a fly to tolerate bacterial infections.
source: Therefore, based on its known functions and the fact that our experimental results follow the predictions of our theoretical model, we propose that Catalase is part of the arsenal that enable a fly to tolerate bacterial infections.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on known Catalase function and experimental results matching model predictions

claim: The SPPL in HIV infections is highly variable among patients.
source: First, it is highly variable among patients
evidence: This is stated as an established observation about HIV infections

claim: The SPPL in HIV infections is heritable, meaning that the SPPL of a newly infected patient positively correlates to that of the person it has been infected by.
source: second, it is heritable, which means that the SPPL of a newly infected patient positively correlates to that of the person it has been infected by.
evidence: This is stated as an established observation about HIV infections

claim: High SPPL in HIV infections is associated to short asymptomatic phases and rapid progression to the final stage of the disease.
source: This is particularly well established in the specific case of HIV infections, where high SPPL is associated to short asymptomatic phases and rapid progression to the final stage of the disease (Fraser et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fraser et al., 2007

claim: Part of the large variance in SPPL could be non-genetic yet heritable.
source: Our model suggests that part of the large variance in SPPL could be non-genetic yet heritable.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on model predictions

claim: If transmission events occur during chronicity, the inoculum size should increase with the SPPL of the donor host.
source: If transmission events occur during chronicity, the inoculum size should indeed increase with the SPPL of the donor host (as suggested by Fraser et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a logical inference supported by citation

claim: The fact that the transient SPPL increases with inoculum size could suffice to create a form of non-genetic heritability in SPPL.
source: As we have demonstrated that the transient SPPL does increase with inoculum size, the SPPL of a newly contaminated host should reflect that of the donor host. The fact that the transient SPPL increases with inoculum size could, therefore, suffice to create a form of non-genetic heritability in SPPL.
evidence: This is an inference from model predictions

claim: Showing that the SPPL is transient informs on the fact that the pathogens, or the damage they cause, obstruct the immune response.
source: Hence, showing that the SPPL is transient informs on the fact that the pathogens, or the damage they cause, obstruct the immune response.
evidence: This is an inference from the model's bistability conditions

claim: Duneau et al., 2017a demonstrated that within-host evolution did not explain bifurcation in their experiments.
source: We did not consider this possibility, first because it is beyond the scope of our study, and second because Duneau et al., 2017a demonstrated that within-host evolution did not explain bifurcation in their experiments.
evidence: Supported by citation to Duneau et al., 2017a

claim: Hosts with an impeded immune response are expected to have a higher PLUD.
source: We conversely predict that hosts with an impeded immune response are expected to have a higher PLUD, which we confirmed with an experimental design more powerful than that of Duneau et al., 2017a (see Figure 8).
evidence: This is a model prediction confirmed by experimental data in Figure 8

claim: Flies injected with large inoculum die faster but at the same load than flies infected with small inoculum.
source: The PLUD, unlike the transient SPPL this time, is independent from inoculum size: flies injected with large inoculum die faster but at the same load than flies infected with small inoculum (Duneau et al., 2017a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Duneau et al., 2017a

claim: The model reproduces the observation that PLUD is independent from inoculum size.
source: Our model reproduces this observation
evidence: This is stated as a model result

claim: The PLUD independence from inoculum size happens because pathogen load is a 'fast variable'.
source: and we have demonstrated mathematically that this happens because pathogen load is a 'fast variable' (Van Kampen, 1985, see Appendix 4).
evidence: This is a mathematical demonstration from the model

claim: Hemocytes have no detectable effects on infections caused by Providencia rettgeri.
source: but hemocytes have no detectable effects on infections caused by Providencia rettgeri (Duneau et al., 2017a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Duneau et al., 2017a

claim: The wound decreases resistance, as indicated by Chambers et al., 2014.
source: Instead, we expect that the wound decreases resistance, as indicated by Chambers et al., 2014.
evidence: Supported by citation to Chambers et al., 2014

claim: Defensin is an antimicrobial peptide strongly upregulated upon P. rettgeri infection.
source: Line A lacks Defensin, an antimicrobial peptide strongly upregulated upon P. rettgeri infection (Duneau et al., 2017b; Troha et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citations to Duneau et al., 2017b and Troha et al., 2018

claim: Defensin has moderate effects on survival in P. rettgeri infections.
source: but with moderate effects on survival (Hanson et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hanson et al., 2019

claim: Lines B and AB, which both lack Diptericins, are expected to be highly susceptible to P. rettgeri.
source: Lines B and AB, which both lack Diptericins, are conversely expected to be highly susceptible to P. rettgeri (Hanson et al., 2019; Unckless et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hanson et al., 2019 and Unckless et al., 2016

claim: BomΔ55C mutants have a PLUD comparable to controls when infected with Enterococcus faecalis.
source: In addition, previous experiments have shown that BomΔ55C mutants have a PLUD comparable to controls when infected with the gram positive bacteria Enterococcus faecalis (Lin et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin et al., 2020

claim: Diptericin A has been shown to be the most active AMP against P. rettgeri.
source: Diptericin A has been shown to be the most active AMP against P. rettgeri
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge

claim: Drosomycin is active mostly against gram positive bacteria and fungi.
source: while Drosomycin is active mostly against gram positive bacteria and fungi.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge

claim: Drosomycin is an antifungi AMP that is inactive against bacteria.
source: Drosomycin being an antifungi AMP that is inactive against bacteria (Fehlbaum et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fehlbaum et al., 1994

claim: Deleting Diptericin A is sufficient to make the mutant more susceptible to the infection than Drs mutant.
source: We found again that death is faster and PLUD higher when Diptericins are deleted (Figure 8D–F; linear mixed model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 10.11, df = 1, p-value = 0.001).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 8D-F

claim: Flies with silenced Diptericin A die faster and at a higher PLUD than controls.
source: We found that flies with silenced Diptericin A die faster and at a higher PLUD than controls (Figure 8G–I; linear mixed model with random experimental blocks: X2 = 8.42, df = 1, p-value = 0.0037).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 8G-I

claim: The log(HR) of silencing Catalase is comparable in strength to that of silencing Diptericin A.
source: The log(HR) is comparable in strength to that of silencing Diptericin A.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing experimental results

claim: The relative difference in PLUD (i.e. log(PLUD ratio)) from silencing Catalase was comparable in strength to that of silencing Diptericin A, but of opposite sign.
source: Again, although the level of PLUD was different, likely due to the difference in genetic background, the relative difference (i.e. log(PLUD ratio)) was comparable in strength to that of silencing Diptericin A, but of opposite sign.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing experimental results
